name: ApeCoin
metaTitle: ApeCoin Casinos: A Volatile Token With One Network
metaDescription: Casinos accepting ApeCoin over Ethereum (ERC20), and the price volatility worth knowing about before holding a balance in it between sessions.
intro:
ApeCoin moves exclusively over Ethereum as an ERC20 token at the casinos that support it, so there is no network choice to make — deposits and withdrawals both use the same rail, with Ethereum mainnet's usual gas costs attached.

The coin itself is considerably more volatile than a major asset like Bitcoin or Ethereum, let alone a stablecoin. That matters specifically for anyone tempted to leave a casino balance sitting in APE for a while: the dollar value of that balance can move meaningfully in either direction between a deposit and a later withdrawal, independent of anything that happens at the casino itself. It is not a criticism of any operator — it is simply what holding a smaller-cap token exposes you to.

Support for ApeCoin is narrower than for the majors on this list; not every crypto casino accepts it, and where it is accepted, liquidity and withdrawal processing can be less battle-tested than for Bitcoin or the leading stablecoins. Worth confirming a casino's own minimum and any withdrawal notes for APE specifically rather than assuming it behaves identically to more established coins on the same platform.

faq.q: Does ApeCoin have multiple networks like USDT?
faq.a: No — it exists as a single ERC20 token on Ethereum, so there is one network to use and no risk of a network mismatch.

faq.q: Is ApeCoin's price stable while held in a casino account?
faq.a: No — it is considerably more volatile than Bitcoin or Ethereum, let alone a stablecoin, so a balance held for a while is exposed to real price movement.
